item.title: BSP Fiji donates $10,000 to Lifeline Fiji to support mental health and suicide prevention efforts
item.description: BSP also sponsored prizes for a youth poster and poem competition organised by Lifeline Fiji volunteers under the themes “Changing the Narrative” and “Lived Experiences.” Leading the BSP delegation, General Manager People and Culture Miliana Susau Tavakaturaga thanked Lifeline Fiji Team Leader Jeremaia Qalobulailakeba Merekula, staff and volunteers for their continued work, particularly in maintai
item.content:encoded:
BSP also sponsored prizes for a youth poster and poem competition organised by Lifeline Fiji volunteers under the themes “Changing the Narrative” and “Lived Experiences.”

Leading the BSP delegation, General Manager People and Culture Miliana Susau Tavakaturaga thanked Lifeline Fiji Team Leader Jeremaia Qalobulailakeba Merekula, staff and volunteers for their continued work, particularly in maintaining a 24/7 support service.

Tavakaturaga says the contribution reflects BSP’s value of caring for people in Fiji who may be silently struggling due to the stigma surrounding mental health.

She says there is a need to move away from a culture of silence and encourage people to know that it is okay to talk, ask for help and have someone willing to listen.

She says BSP is also focused on supporting the wellbeing of its own employees by creating a workplace where staff feel valued, understood and supported.

Merekula thanked BSP for its continued support since the partnership began in 2016.

He says when BSP first supported Lifeline Fiji, the organisation was facing serious challenges and was close to shutting down.

Merekula says the need for Lifeline Fiji’s services remains high, especially between September and December when the organisation receives a significant increase in calls.

He says changing the narrative means creating a society where people feel comfortable speaking up and where someone is ready to listen.

During the event, participants lit candles and observed a minute of silence to remember Fijians who have lost their lives to suicide.

Merekula says over the past five years since 2020, 489 Fijians have died by suicide, with 76 percent being males.

He says 13 young Fijians aged between 18 and 24 years have died by suicide this year.

Merekula adds that for every suicide, there are an estimated 20 others who attempt to take their own lives, highlighting the important role Lifeline Fiji plays in providing support to those who are struggling.

Lifeline Fiji operates a 24/7 service and continues to strengthen its capacity through support from Lifeline Australia, including training and exchange programmes.

The organisation will continue its World Suicide Prevention Day activities throughout the month with initiatives such as the Community Kitchen and “Choosing Tomorrow”, which encourages people experiencing distress to find hope and reasons to continue living.

item.title: 7 jobs created after opening of new restaurant in Labasa
item.description: Karishma Kumari , Mohammed Feroz · 14/09/2026 Seven new jobs have been created following the opening of the Fry Master Restaurant in Tuatua, Labasa, as the business looks to meet growing demand for dining options outside Labasa Town.
item.content:encoded:
Karishma Kumari , Mohammed Feroz · 14/09/2026

Seven new jobs have been created following the opening of the Fry Master Restaurant in Tuatua, Labasa, as the business looks to meet growing demand for dining options outside Labasa Town.

Restaurant owner Ashneel Sharma says the decision to open the restaurant in Tuatua was driven by high demand from customers, particularly those travelling between Labasa and Savusavu who have limited restaurant options outside Labasa Town.

Sharma says traffic congestion and limited parking in Labasa also made it difficult for customers to access restaurants in the town area.

He says locating Fry Master outside the Labasa Town boundary provides customers with another option that is easier to access.

Sharma says affordability is also a key focus of the business, with the restaurant aiming to keep its food prices lower compared to other restaurants and to provide delivery services to customers within a 10-kilometre radius.

He adds finding a suitable location was one of the biggest challenges he faced while trying to establish the restaurant.

He says despite this initial difficulty, he remained determined to establish the business.

item.title: Cakacaka takes helm as General Manager of Nanuku Resort Fiji
item.description: Fijian hospitality leader Vuli Cakacaka has been appointed General Manager of Nanuku Resort Fiji. Cakacaka, who was born on Vatoa in the Lau Group and raised in Suva, has more than 23 years of experience in the hospitality industry, working across Fiji and international markets.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian hospitality leader Vuli Cakacaka has been appointed General Manager of Nanuku Resort Fiji.

Cakacaka, who was born on Vatoa in the Lau Group and raised in Suva, has more than 23 years of experience in the hospitality industry, working across Fiji and international markets.

He brings extensive experience and leadership expertise to the position.

He joined Nanuku Resort Fiji as Resort Manager in 2024 and will now oversee all aspects of resort operations, guest experience and financial performance as General Manager.

Cakacaka says the true strength of a resort lies in the people who deliver the experience.

He says he is honoured to lead the team and build on the strong foundation already established at Nanuku while continuing to provide personalised luxury.

He says the resort will continue creating meaningful experiences for guests while celebrating Fiji's culture, people and natural beauty.

Cakacaka is also committed to developing Fijian hospitality professionals and creating opportunities for local talent.

Storey Hospitality Co-founder and Managing Partner Michael Casey says Cakacaka's extensive experience, understanding of Fijian hospitality and people-first leadership make him the right person to lead the resort.

Casey says they look forward to the continued growth and success of Nanuku under Cakacaka's leadership.

Located on Fiji's southern coast in Pacific Harbour, Nanuku Resort Fiji is celebrated for its luxury experiences, authentic cultural connections and exceptional service.

The resort remains dedicated to delivering unforgettable stays while championing sustainability, community engagement and world-class hospitality.
